messages:
mariam: Quick RFC follow-up — propose a feature-flagged coexistence window for the /v1 -> /v2 contract change. Plan: gateway accepts both shapes for 12 weeks behind a tenant opt-in flag, emit telemetry, then start strict reject after warning period. Thoughts?

alex: I like opt-in first. Can we avoid per-tenant shims in the runtime? That was a lot of overhead last time.

mariam: Good call. Gateway-only shim for the first phase, runtime will only get a compatibility toggle for traffic routed by gateway.

priya: How will clients opt in? Header, param, or admin UI? We need an automated signal to turn on for tenants who pass compatibility tests.

jon: Header + admin flag. Header example: `X-Redwood-Compat: v1` from clients. Admin side sets tenant flag `compat_v1=true` and gateway rewrites body to v2 shape.

miguel: +1. Also propose a fallback circuit: if gateway detects >5% error rate for rewritten requests in 5m window, it auto-rolls back for that tenant and alerts.

mariam: Draft nginx snippet for rewrite (gateway edge):
```
if ($http_x_redwood_compat = "v1") {
  proxy_set_header X-RI-Rewrite "v1->v2";
  # payload transform via edge filter
}
```

priya: We'll need telemetry fields: `compat_flag`, `rewrite_applied`, `rewrite_error`, `origin_version`. Add to rollout dashboard.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: compat-gateway-filter v0.1 -> staging (sha: abcd123).

alex: Can we ensure auth tokens remain compatible? v2 moves to scoped tokens. Gateway must translate unscoped->scoped claims for the shim.

jon: Agreed. We'll add a translation layer that checks `x-auth-version` and maps scopes; keep exact audit logs of mapped claims.

mariam: Ok action items: (1) Gateway shim PR (edge filter + header) @miguel (2) Telemetry + dashboard @priya (3) Token-translation spec @jon (4) Runtime opt-in toggle no-op for now @alex. We'll run a 12-week window with telemetry gates at weeks 2/6/10.

priya: Also add a tiny bake: enable for 5% tenants first day, 25% week 1, then ramp.

miguel: I'll open the PRs today.

alex: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
